concept_title: 보랏빛 달밤의 매화 무대, 뱀과 렌
revision_note: V1 (2ac3ad0) rejected by the owner: too many borders. V2 (73a2823) merged the sky, both lattice doors and the moon/cloud layer into one back plate, shrank the clear rim 2.5 -> 1.0 mm and rendered clear acrylic see-through in the assembly preview. V3 (657a484) recomposed the scene but the owner prefers V2 ("v2가 낫다고 한거야"). V4 (a2a83cd) = V2 plus two owner requests: the blossom tree printed diagonally into the back panel and Len "seated" by cropping her raster at the seat line. V5 (7459c7f) restructured the scene (Len whole on a 70 mm serpent's coil, the tree back as ONE cut plate whose 2.5 mm canopy envelope webbed the blossoms together with clear acrylic) and the owner rejected it ("이거 아니야 v4에서 잘림 문제만 해결하고 나무를 예시 이미지처럼 대각선 배치 해달라고"). V6 (62963a8) = V4 with exactly those two changes: Len shown whole on the base line and the tree printed into the back panel, leaning up to the right like the concept. V7 = the owner's decision on the tree ("벚꽃하고 나무는 별도 에셋으로 분리해줘"): the tree is no longer printed on the back panel and is no longer one clear-webbed piece. 03_blossom_tree.png is split by colour into (a) a TREE cut piece = the dark trunk and branches (wood pixels; twigs thinner than 0.5 mm pruned so every feature is at least 2.5 mm after the 1.0 mm rim) standing on its own tab on its own depth row (31) with its base behind the serpent, and (b) six BLOSSOM cut pieces = pink petal clusters grouped around branch tips (5 mm sky gaps between clusters), each a separate plate with a 1.0 mm rim, no clear webbing between clusters, mounted on the base BEHIND the tree plate on two depth rows (39 and 47) on a 12.25 mm clear stem so the branches cross in front of them and the gaps between clusters show the sky and moon like the concept. Everything else is V6 exactly: whole seated Len, serpent, moon, doors, base, layout, rims. V8 = the owner's correction ("벚꽃-나무는 하나여야지" - the blossom tree must be ONE piece; "저 문" - the assets he wanted separate are the doors): (1) the TREE is ONE cut piece with the complete tree printed on it (trunk, branches and all blossom clusters); the the opaque mask opened 1.5 mm is the cut skeleton so the gaps between branch/cluster groups are real cut-out openings (sky and moon show through, no clear canopy fill, no stems, no cluster plates); the printed branch skeleton connects every part, twig connectors are widened to 2.75 mm of clear acrylic so every cut feature meets the 2.5 mm minimum after the 1.0 mm rim, and gaps that cannot be real openings (under 2.5 mm after the rim) stay printed with the back panel's blurred local colour instead of clear acrylic; placement, rotation, scale and row are V7's. (2) The DOORS become their own cut pieces: the two lattice doorways of 06_lattice_doors.png (85 mm art, 1.0 mm rim, lattice openings) stand on 18 mm tabs at row 47 exactly where V2-V7 printed them; the back panel loses the printed doors and keeps the sky, moon, clouds and waves, with the sky/wave art mirrored into the former door zones. Whole Len, serpent, moon, base, slots, rims 1.0 mm and the layout stay V7/V6 exactly: 7 pieces, 8 slots, rows 12/23/31/47/56. V9 = the owner's final tweaks ("마지막 수정 문하고 배경 높이만 좀 맞춰주고 벛꽃나무는 문하고 캐릭터사이 왼쪽으로 빼봐": match the doors to the backdrop height; pull the blossom tree out to the left, between the door and the character). (1) DOOR HEIGHT = BACKDROP HEIGHT: both lattice door plates are scaled from 85 mm to 89.57 mm art (1.0538x) so each door's cut top stands at 92.0 mm above the base top, exactly the back panel's cut top (95.0 mm assembled: 3 base + 1.0 bottom rim + 90 art + 1.0 top rim; the V8 report's 94.0 / 88.8 mm counted the top rim only and omitted the 1.0 mm rim under every plate, so V9 reports the real cut tops). Same tab axis (x 55.5 / 224.5, row 47), same slots, 1.0 mm rim, both doors symmetric about the scene axis; no lattice hole reaches 2.5 mm even at the larger size, so the lattice stays printed. (2) TREE MOVED LEFT: the one-piece tree (V8 design unchanged: same 35 deg clockwise rotation, same cut skeleton = the opaque mask opened 1.5 mm at the 88 mm reference scale, same 22 cluster connectors, same rim/closing/opening rules) stands in the gap between the LEFT DOOR and LEN with its trunk base at scene x 96 (row 31, tab moved from x 131), behind the serpent. The 88 mm tree (95 mm wide) cannot fit that 63 mm gap without overlapping the door or Len, so it is scaled to 56.0 mm art (0.636x) - the largest size that keeps at least 1.0 mm of clear space between the tree's cut and the door's and Len's cuts; the canopy no longer crosses behind Len. Everything else is V8 exactly: whole seated Len, serpent, backdrop art, base, slots (one slot moved with the tree), 1.0 mm rims, rows 12/23/31/47/56.

finished_size_mm.note: 3T: base 3 + back panel plate 92.0 above the base top (1.0 mm rim under the art + 90 art + 1.0 mm rim) = 95.0 mm; V8 reported 94.0 by omitting the bottom rim. V9 door plates match it: cut top 92.0 mm above the base top (89.57 mm art + rims), 95.0 mm assembled, tops aligned with the back panel. The one-piece tree (56.0 mm art at scene x 96) tops out at 50.7 mm above the base top (53.7 mm assembled).

clear_border_rationale: docs/laser-cut-quality.md fixes no rim minimum; its hard limits are the 0.035 mm curve deviation and the 12 mm load-path floor on the buffered silhouette. 1.0 mm is the smallest round offset that still keeps UV ink 0.5 mm inside the cut edge under a 0.5 mm print registration error. V9 keeps 1.0 mm on every plate. The one-piece tree and the doors add material only where the laser rules need it: a 1.25 mm closing after the rim removes sky slits under 2.5 mm (needle gaps), and the tree's twig connectors are 2.75 mm wide (1.375 mm of clear acrylic around the printed twig) so the measured minimum feature is at least 2.5 mm everywhere.

extend_sky_mm.note: V8: the two lattice doors are no longer printed on the back panel; the sky/wave raster (1423 px = 138.6 mm at 90 mm) is widened by mirroring its own edge columns (312 px = 30.4 mm on the left, 313 px = 30.5 mm on the right, exactly the widths the printed doors had in V7) so the plate keeps its V7 outline and the waves and stars continue into the former door zones without resampling.

overlays.note: moon and both cloud islands (including V1's unused 34 x 6.9 mm upper-right cloud) registered over the sky as in V2/V4

pieces.note: V8: sky + moon/clouds only. The lattice doors that V2-V7 printed at its sides are now the door_left and door_right cut pieces standing in front of it at row 47; the sky/wave art is extended into their former zones (see extend_sky_mm). Moon and clouds registered 5 mm below the sky top exactly as V2-V7.

V9 owner request ("벛꽃나무는 문하고 캐릭터사이 왼쪽으로 빼봐"): the same one-piece tree as V8 (trunk, branches and every blossom cluster printed with the original pixels, dark wood + pink blossoms, 35 deg clockwise) moved out of Len's background into the gap between the LEFT DOOR and LEN, its trunk base at scene x ~96 on row 31 behind the serpent (the slot moves with it; the V8 slot at x 131 is removed). The V8 cut skeleton (opaque mask opened 1.5 mm at the 88 mm reference scale: which twigs and petals are cut) is carried unchanged and scaled to 56.0 mm art, because the 88 mm tree (95 mm wide) cannot fit the 63 mm gap between the door and Len without overlapping them; 56.0 mm (0.636x) is the largest size that keeps at least 1.0 mm between the tree's cut and the door's and Len's cuts. Rim 1.0 mm, closing 1.25 mm, connectors 2.75 mm and the 2.5 mm opening rule are applied in millimetres at the new size, so the plate keeps every hard rule; the canopy no longer crosses behind Len toward the right and ends at x ~135.3, 1.3 mm short of Len's cut; its right half stands behind the serpent's body as in V8 (the serpent is on row 23, the tree on row 31).

V9 owner request ("문하고 배경 높이만 좀 맞춰주고"): the left lattice doorway of 06_lattice_doors.png scaled from 85 mm to 89.57 mm art (1.0538x; 32.0 mm wide) so the plate's cut top stands at 92.0 mm above the base top = the back panel's cut top (95.0 mm assembled; V8 reached 87.45 / 90.45 mm). V8 asset rules unchanged: 1.0 mm rim, thin frame features widened to the 2.5 mm minimum, the lattice printed and its holes printed with the back panel's blurred local colour because none is 2.5 mm wide after the rim. Same tab axis (x 55.5, row 47) and slot as V8, so the door grows symmetrically about its V2-V8 printed position (scene x 37.8-73.1 cut).

V9: the right lattice doorway (30.5 x 85 mm art in V8) scaled to 89.57 mm art (32.1 mm wide), cut top 92.0 mm above the base top like the back panel and the left door; 1.0 mm rim, 18 mm tab at row 47 on the same axis (x 224.5) and slot as V8, mirroring door_left.

V4 position and scale unchanged (55 mm at x=115, row 23). Not bent or moved: its coil ends at x=138, z=8-21 and cannot reach Len's hips (x=152-170, z=33) without a major reshape, which the owner did not ask for.

V6 owner request (fix the cropping): the whole 84 mm figure at V4's scale, x and row - no crop_below_fraction. Her long leg's boot sole is the lowest ink, so both boot rims rest on the base line 1.0 mm (rim) above the base top, the sword tip 3 mm above it and the hips (crotch line) 33 mm above it; the pose (one leg hanging to the base, one knee raised, sword down-left) reads as seated on the base edge. The tab under the art centre sits between the two boots where the buffered silhouette is narrower than the 12 mm load-path floor, so the bud guard raises a 12.25 mm clear riser inside the tab window from the base line up to where the legs close (about 9 mm); it is the only clear support and carries no print.

front_view_policy.note: ORIGIN is a deliberately stacked centre scene (doors and tree behind the serpent and character, tree across the moon): polygon occlusion is by design and overstates visual blocking. Numbers are recorded per piece in validation_report.json; composition acceptance is the vision-checked assembly preview against the supplied concept art and the V7 preview. Structural checks (row clearance, overhang, load path, gaps, rims, minimum feature, openings) stay hard.

board_layout_note: Product master board 340 x 420 mm: back panel top-left, character lower-left, the two door plates centre-left, serpent right, the one-piece tree right-centre; the A3 stage re-nests the same cut polygons at a 3 mm gap.

tree_one_piece.scale_note: 56.0 mm art (0.636x the V8 size; unrotated alpha box 1283 x 990 px = 449 ppi at this size, embedded at the native pixels, never upscaled): the largest size whose cut keeps at least 1.0 mm from the door's and Len's cuts when the trunk base stands at scene x 96 in the gap between the left door and Len. V8's 88 mm art made a 95 mm wide plate that cannot fit the 63 mm gap.
tree_one_piece.trunk_rule: the tab axis is the lowest wood pixel of the rotated tree (wood = opaque pixel that is not red-dominant: r - max(g, b) < 45 or r < 110), i.e. the trunk base; V9 places it at scene x 96 (row 31) in the gap between the left door and the serpent.
tree_one_piece.skeleton_rule: opaque = alpha > 128 on the native-resolution 35 deg clockwise rotation. The cut skeleton is the V8 design carried unchanged: the opaque mask opened with a 1.5 mm radius at the 88 mm reference scale (skeleton_ref_mm), so exactly the twigs and petals V8 cut are cut here, scaled to the V9 art height; the rim (1.0 mm), closing (1.25 mm), connectors (2.75 mm) and the 2.5 mm opening rule are applied in millimetres at the V9 size. Main component plus every detached component of at least 2 mm2 is kept; smaller specks are cut away.
tree_one_piece.connector_rule: each detached component is attached to the main skeleton along its own twig: the geodesic path inside the opaque mask from the fragment to the main component is buffered to 2.75 mm (the twig is printed inside the clear connector). Measured minimum feature of every connector >= 2.5 mm. The twig path is Gaussian-smoothed (sigma 2 px) and simplified (0.15 mm) before buffering so the laser path stays within the segment gate.
tree_one_piece.opening_rule: the cut body is skeleton + connectors, buffered 1.0 mm and closed 1.25 mm (sky slits under 2.5 mm filled). Enclosed holes at least 2.5 mm wide (erosion test) are kept as cut-out openings unless they would leave a neck under 2.5 mm or cross the riser; every other enclosed gap stays solid and is PRINTED with the back panel's blurred local colour (no clear acrylic fill inside the piece apart from the 1.0 mm rim, the connectors and the riser).
tree_one_piece.print_rule: the print is the original RGBA pixels inside the body 0.6 mm from every cut edge and opening (riser left clear); every enclosed gap - everything inside the piece that is not printed art, not the 1.0 mm clear band along a cut edge and not a clear connector halo - is printed with the back panel's tone sampled at the same scene position (extended sky raster Gaussian-blurred over 15 mm so waves and stars average into the gradient, plus the moon/cloud layer as one uniform pale colour through its own blurred mask), so the gaps read as the sky or moon behind them with no wave line, cloud edge or crater baked into the plate; the asset's semi-transparent fringes print only inside those gaps; nothing prints outside the body, so twigs and petals the cut skeleton dropped never print inside an opening and the outer rim stays clear.

doors.rule: each door island (alpha silhouette at 89.57 mm art) buffered 1.0 mm, closed 1.25 mm, thin features widened to the 2.5 mm minimum and re-closed; enclosed lattice holes at least 2.5 mm wide after the rim are cut-out openings (none qualifies even at 89.57 mm), every other lattice gap is printed with the back panel's blurred local colour. One 18 mm tab under the art centre, row 47. V9: 89.57 mm art (1.0538x the V8 85 mm) puts the cut top at 92.0 mm above the base top, the back panel's cut top, so the doors stand as tall as the backdrop with their tops aligned.

tree_one_piece.clearance_rule: V9: the tree's standing cut must keep at least this distance from the standing cuts of the character (row 12) and both door plates (row 47) in the front view - the owner asked for the tree between the door and Len without overlapping either. The serpent (row 23) stands in front of the tree by design (V8 rule), so the trunk base is judged on its printed ink: at least the same clearance from the serpent's printed ink near the base line (z <= 8 mm); the clear rims of the two plates may cross there (reported).
